NEWTON, Mass.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Bright Horizons Family Solutions® Inc. (NYSE: BFAM), a leading provider of high-quality education and care solutions designed to help employers support employees across life and career stages, today announced financial results for the second quarter of 2021.
Second Quarter 2021 Highlights (compared to second quarter 2020):
Revenue of $441 million (increase of 50%)
Income from operations of $34 million (increase of 319%)
Net income of $19 million and diluted earnings per common share of $0.31 (increases of $18 million and $0.30, respectively)
Non-GAAP measures
Adjusted income from operations* of $34 million (increase of 25%)
Adjusted EBITDA* of $68 million (increase of 13%)
Adjusted net income* of $30 million and diluted adjusted earnings per common share* of $0.49 (increases of 13% and 11%, respectively)
“ I am pleased to report another solid quarter across all of our services, as we continue to make good progress in returning our business to pre-COVID-19 levels,” said Stephen Kramer, Chief Executive Officer. “ With full-time enrollment and back-up usage returning, and most centers re-opening by this fall, our recovery from the pandemic is on track. I continue to be inspired by our dedicated teachers and center operations leadership, who have been supporting children and families through these very challenging times, and likewise am proud of the strong client partnerships that have enabled the delivery of impactful solutions to families and learners over the past 18 months.”
Second Quarter 2021 Results
Revenue increased $147.7 million, or 50%, in the second quarter of 2021 from the second quarter of 2020, primarily attributable to enrollment increases in our open child care centers and the re-opening of our temporarily closed child care centers. While enrollment in our child care centers continued to improve during the quarter, our centers are still operating below pre-COVID-19 enrollment levels during this re-ramping phase. The increase in revenue in the full service center-based child care segment was partially offset by decreases in our back-up care services compared to the same period in the prior year. While we had gains from expanded back-up care client sales and increased utilization in traditional in-center and in-home care during the quarter, back-up care revenue decreased compared to the prior year as the second quarter in 2020 benefited from significant demand (primarily for self-sourced reimbursed care) during the early stages of the pandemic when other care alternatives were not available.
Income from operations was $34.0 million for the second quarter of 2021 compared to $8.1 million for the same period in 2020. The increase in income from operations reflects improved gross profit contributions in the full service center-based child care segment arising from higher enrollment as centers re-ramp and the re-opening of our temporarily closed centers, partially offset by reduced contributions from our back-up care services, which benefited in the second quarter of 2020 from increased demand during the early stages of the pandemic. Net income was $18.8 million for the second quarter of 2021 compared to net income of $0.4 million in the same 2020 period, an increase of $18.4 million due to the increase in income from operations, partially offset by a higher effective tax rate. Diluted earnings per common share was $0.31 for the second quarter of 2021 compared to $0.01 for the second quarter of 2020.

Daniel Houghton became the CEO of the popular travel publishing company, Lonely Planet, at just 24. The company wasn’t adapting to modern times and its future looked bleak. They needed someone young, someone who knew how to transition Loney Planet into the digital age, and someone who understood both media and technology. That’s when Houghton was tapped to lead the company. Under his leadership, the company modernized and developed a new generation of readers, and now has over 16.2 million followers on social media. Recently, Houghton stepped down as CEO and wrote the book Wherever You Go, which has just been released. I had the chance to sit down with him and ask about his time at Lonely Planet, his new book, and his future.
You became the CEO of Lonely Planet, one of the largest travel companies in the world, at just 24 years old. What was that like?
Well… the company didn’t exactly come with its own guidebook (laughs). It was really rough in the beginning. I come from a media background, but I had never had such responsibility before. It’s a huge company, but luckily, they have such a great team and it really became a group effort. But yeah.. there was a very steep learning curve for sure.
Did you enjoy your time there?
Oh, of course! I mean, it’s such an amazing company, it has a huge dedicated fanbase around the world, and travel is something I’m so passionate about. We hired people who loved the brand and loved travel, not people who were chasing money, and that made the entire company glow with such incredible energy.
You ended up stepping down from Lonely Planet, moved out to a farm in Tennessee and wrote a book. Explain how that happened.
Running a major company like Lonely Planet takes a lot out of you. It was an intense amount of travel and an intense amount of responsibility. We have a huge team that’s spread out all over the world. I spent about 200-250 days per year on the road, which I absolutely loved and it was amazing, but it also has a way of wearing you out. By the end, after the company had made such growth, I felt that I had left my mark. I had made some really good things happen and it just felt like it was the right time to start a new journey.
And unfortunately, then my dad got really sick, which I talk about in the forward of my book. So, I really wanted to be able to be close to my family. The farm thing came from me always wanting to live on a farm. I love woodworking, I love dogs, I love being outside, really, I just like a lot of old man things I guess! But yeah, with my dad being sick, I wanted some time off. I wanted to be with my family as much as I could. So now we all live in the same area and I can see them as much I want.

The Buccaneers didn’t play in Week 13. Which means that there was no reason for Buccaneers coach Bruce Arians to directly criticize (a/k/a be honest) or to passive-aggressively snipe at quarterback Tom Brady. Instead, Arians heaped praise on Brady.
“It’s been fantastic,” Arians told reporters when asked about working with Brady. “From day one, getting him here [and] watching him prepare and help young players get better. He’s a joy to coach and he’s a fantastic competitor. I love that about him. He’s been there and done it and he’s helped so many of our guys who haven’t [been there] believe that they can. That’s a huge part of it and I couldn’t ask any more out of him.”
Arians also praised Brady’s overall ability to show up and work every day, despite being 43.
“I don’t see any drop at all,” Arians said. “I’ve had some veteran guys that needed Wednesdays off and he’s not one of those guys. He’s amazing that way and how he takes care of himself. He’s helped a lot of young players learn about taking care of themselves also.”
Brady’s leadership and experience likewise was praised.
“There’s no doubt about it,” Arians said. “I’ve been very, very fortunate with some of the best quarterbacks that all have that. Every single one I’ve probably ever coached have had that ability. Peyton [Manning], Ben [Roethlisberger], Andrew Luck as a rookie was amazing. Tom [Brady], Timmy Couch, Kelly Holcomb — every one of those guys that were successful. When they got in the huddle, they had the ability to make everybody believe that this is the best play that’s going to be called and run. Then, walk off, work with guys, take them to the side, work with them and bring them along. All those great ones do it.”
Arians also didn’t take the bait when asked whether he’s frustrated with the offense’s inability to properly execute the scripted plays to start the game.

PYONGYANG, North Korea (AP) -- International Olympic Committee President Thomas Bach has met with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in Pyongyang.
Bach told an Associated Press Television crew the two had a 30-minute formal meeting followed by 45 minutes of casual talking while watching a football match Friday afternoon at Pyongyang's huge May Day Stadium. He said Kim supports a plan to have North Korean athletes compete in the 2020 Tokyo Summer Olympics and the 2022 Beijing Winter Games.
Bach arrived in Pyongyang on Thursday to discuss development of sports in North Korea and the preparation of its athletes to qualify and participate in upcoming Olympics. He is the first foreign official to meet Kim since the North Korean leader returned from a summit in Beijing with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

The Golden Knights have boldly gone where no other U.S.-based NHL team has this season: Canada.

The Knights stayed awhile the last time they went to Canada.
They were in the NHL’s secure zone in Edmonton, Alberta, for 51 days for the 2020 postseason during their run to the Western Conference Final.

Opener Lizelle Lee smashed a blistering century before South African bowlers put up an outstanding effort to register an emphatic 113-run victory over debutant Thailand in the ICC Women’s T20 World Cup at the Manuka Oval in Canberra on Friday.
Electing to bat, the Proteas posted 195 for three, the highest team total in the tournament’s history, on the back of opener Lee’s 60-ball 101 and Sune Luus’ unbeaten 61. In response, Thailand was bundled out for 82 in 19.1 overs.
With the win, South Africa strengthened its grip on Group B as it gets ready to take on Pakistan on Sunday with the semifinals in sight. Thailand, which has a knack for nabbing early wickets, was gifted one when Dane van Niekerk (2) patted Ratanporn Padunglerd’s full toss to mid-on.
Lee, 10th in the ICC T20I batting rankings, dominated the scoring and slog swept Onnicha Kamchomphu for a 75-metre six. Thailand was forced to use seven different bowlers inside nine overs but none could withstand Lee's assault. She reached her 50 from 35 balls with a straight six.

24-year-old Luus, featuring in her fourth women’s T20 World Cup, then swung Chanida Sutthiruang’s full toss for six over fine leg. Lee came in without a half-century in nine international innings but glided towards a century in 59 balls, showing her touch with a late cut for four before bringing up a ton fittingly with a four.
Immediately after raising her bat to salute a jubilant South Africa dugout, she chipped a catch back to Suleeporn Laomi to end the partnership at 131.

Retired off-spinner Graeme Swann had bemoaned England's indifferent approach towards slow bowling before the five-match series started and his fears were confirmed after the touring side were handed a 4-0 drubbing.
The alarm bells would have been ringing when England's spinners were out-bowled in Bangladesh in October, where the side lost their first ever test against the hosts in a series regarded by many as an appetiser for the Indian leg of the trip.

Footwear supplier Pou Chen Corp (寶成工業) yesterday reported a net profit of NT$12.92 billion (US$443.18 million) for last year, down 1 percent from NT$13.06 billion in 2016, mainly due to higher expenses to expand and renovate its retail business.
Earnings per share were NT$4.38, down slightly from NT$4.43 in 2016, the company said in a statement.
Revenue totaled NT$278.63 billion, up 1.4 percent from NT$274.9 billion the previous year, while gross margin rose to 26.2 percent from 25.6 percent, the statement showed.
However, operating expenses over the period increased 6.5 percent to NT$56 billion, while operating profit decreased 4 percent to NT$17.7 billion.
Expenses rose because of an ongoing plan to expand its distribution channels and revamp some of its existing stores, the company said.
Pou Chen, the world’s largest branded athletic and casual footwear maker, operates its sportswear retail business in China through its Hong Kong-listed subsidiary, Pou Sheng International Ltd (寶勝國際).
Footwear manufacturing accounted for 70 percent of its revenue last year, while its retail business made up the remaining 30 percent.

Fans of Dave Chappelle's Comedy Central series Chappelle's Show will be surprised if they go to watch the stand-up comedian's sketch show on Netflix tonight. Why? Because Chappelle's Show has been removed from the streaming platform. The comedy series was released on both Netflix (and HBO Max) on November 1 — a huge move for the comedian who has had a multi-special deal with the streamer for years. Chappelle even mentioned this big release event during his opening monologue while hosting the most recent episode of Saturday Night Live.
But things have taken a turn in the weeks since Chappelle's Show hit Netflix and HBO Max. On Tuesday, Chappelle uploaded a video to his Instagram titled "Unforgiven." The 18-minute video appears to have been shot during a recent set of Chappelle's. Over the course of 18 minutes, Chappelle confirms he is the one who initiated the move to have Chappelle's Show removed from Netflix. He tied the show's removal from Netflix to ongoing issues with ViacomCBS and Comedy Central, who he claims did not pay him as part of the show's licensing contract.
In the video, Chappelle outlines his history of clashes with Viacom and why he left Chappelle's Show in 2005, saying, "If you are streaming that show, you are fencing stolen goods. They stole that (show) from me, they just took it," later going on to say, "I found out these people were streaming my work and never had to ask me or they never had to tell me. Perfectly legal because I signed the contract, but is that right? I didn’t think so."
Image via Netflix
Chappelle then offered thanks to Netflix for honoring his request to have the show removed, sharing with the audience, "(Netflix) agreed that they would take it off their platform just so I could feel better. That’s why I [work] with Netflix because they pay me my money, they do what they say they are going to do and they went above and beyond what you could expect from a businessman."
The veteran stand-up made an appeal to his audience in an effort to drive home his pain and disappointment with his treatment at the hands of Viacom: "So I’m not going to the agents, I’m coming to my real boss — I’m coming to you. I’m begging you — if you ever liked me, if you ever think there was anything worthwhile about me, I’m begging you, please don’t watch that show.

A standing COVID-19 vaccine clinic at La Palmera and a program to vaccinate homeless people are in the works, Corpus Christi and Nueces County officials said Thursday.
The La Palmera clinic will launch Tuesday and will be open Monday through Sunday during regular mall hours, public health director Annette Rodriguez said during the city and county’s weekly COVID-19 briefing.
People can pre-register or register on site, Rodriguez said. Officials hope to have at least 100 doses available every day.
To pre-register, visit cctexas.com/vaccineregistration or call 361-561-1101.
The clinic will be in the former Charming Charlie location near Grimaldi’s, Rodriguez said.
The mall is “a place that most of us might go anyway,” Nueces County Judge Barbara Canales said. “Whether you’re shopping or dining or getting your free, life-saving COVID-19 vaccine shot, it sounds like it’s a good day to be at La Palmera.
“La Palmera will be part of the many tools we have to fight back against this horrible disease.”
Homeless population
With shipments of Johnson and Johnson on the way, the city is working with providers of homeless services to identify the best way to reach that population, city spokeswoman Christian Cabazos said.
Unlike the two-dose vaccines by Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna, the Johnson and Johnson vaccine requires only one dose. Experts say that makes it an ideal option for hard-to-reach populations.
“Your city and your health district are working to ensure that all populations have access to the vaccine,” Cabazos said.
Save Our Seniors
Registration for the Save Our Seniors vaccination program will open at noon Friday.

Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) is the best known of the cryptocurrencies, and it's seen a rapid increase in price since the virtual coin was introduced. Many prominent financial experts have endorsed investing some money in Bitcoin, including Dave Ramsey and Suze Orman.
But even if putting some money into Bitcoin could potentially be a valid investment approach, you definitely shouldn't make it the centerpiece of your retirement saving efforts. Here's why.
You need to diversify, even with Bitcoin
Bitcoin has seen explosive gains since the virtual coin was created, and there's definitely an argument to be made that you could make a lot of money by investing in it.
But the problem is that its real-world utility is still currently limited, and it has a relatively short track record compared to many other assets you could invest in. It's impossible to know what the future holds for Bitcoin. And with the coins only having value because people believe they do, there's a very real chance that an investment in Bitcoin could end up being a loser over the long term.
While Bitcoin may be riskier than many other investments, such as index funds or stocks in established companies, that's not the only reason you shouldn't count on it to make you a retired millionaire. You shouldn't base your entire retirement portfolio around any single investment, whether Bitcoin or shares of Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) or even an S&P 500 index fund.
That's because putting all of your eggs in one basket is simply too risky when it comes to retirement. Retirees cannot live on Social Security alone as it is meant to replace just 40% of your pre-retirement earnings. You need to have a sizable nest egg to cover the necessities without a lot of financial struggle, so you need a retirement portfolio that doesn't expose you to too much risk.
The best way to build such a portfolio is to invest in a wide mix of assets, including stocks, bonds, index funds -- and cryptocurrencies, if you're interested in buying them.

CHENNAI: Inscryption is really a nerdy puzzle-based deck-building game. It is based off a simple boardgame mechanic, which works surprisingly well as a videogame. What reeled me in, is its lore and the very peculiar, nightmare-esque aesthetic. I am in a cabin, the door is locked. The room is cloaked in darkness, and I only see a table, dimly lit by cursed candles that indicate my fate. On the other end of the table is a bearded stranger, with skeletal fingers and bright eyes. He immerses me into the illusion he has woven.
I am told that I am in a forest, in a caravan. The cards are my guardian creatures that help me struggle ahead. There are helpful witches, greedy hunters, and the occasional packrats. I must use the boons they give me to my advantage. I believe everything the stranger tells me. He challenges me to an insane card game. I must play, and I must win. Or I lose, and start from the beginning all over again.
To a person with no context, the cards would appear as though speaking a whole other language. But Inscryption does an excellent job of visually explaining the game mechanics.The game begins with a starter deck of woodland creatures. There are squirrels, and then other creatures. Squirrels could be sacrificed to give powers to the other creatures. The creatures would then attack the enemy, enough to tip over his damage scales — and make him lose.

# Body Cameras for Police: A Complex Balance of Oversight and Local Control

*A Reuters Special Report*

At the NYPD police academy in Queens, New York, a police officer demonstrates a body camera during a news conference on the "Big Brother" pilot program involving 60 officers. The December 2014 initiative would later influence nationwide discussions on police accountability.

Civil rights advocates and law enforcement leaders are raising concerns about President Obama's $75 million proposal to equip local police departments with 50,000 body cameras. They emphasize that without robust oversight mechanisms, the technology's deployment could potentially undermine, rather than strengthen, public trust in law enforcement.

The proposal, which emerged following the Ferguson grand jury decision not to indict a white officer in the shooting death of an unarmed Black teenager, requires congressional approval. While it mandates department training and Justice Department guidance, questions remain about enforcement mechanisms.

## The Oversight Challenge

Barbara Arnwine, executive director of the Lawyers' Committee on Civil Rights, emphasizes the critical nature of accountability: "Without proper enforcement of disciplinary measures, body cameras become meaningless tools, especially in departments with poor track records."

Daytona Beach Police Chief Michael Chitwood's experience illustrates this concern. Having implemented body cameras since 2010, he recently dismissed an officer for deactivating their camera during a violent incident. Chitwood advocates for strong federal guidelines that can withstand local political pressures and union influence.

However, not all law enforcement leaders share this perspective. Greenville Police Chief Ken Miller argues for local autonomy: "Every community has unique challenges and dynamics that require tailored approaches."

## Implementation Hurdles

The Police Executive Research Forum's recent study revealed that among 63 agencies using body cameras, one-third lack written policies governing their use. Critical questions remain unresolved:

- Privacy concerns in private residences
- Data storage duration
- Public access to footage
- Mandatory activation protocols

Research from Arizona State University demonstrates the impact of clear policies: officers are 20% more likely to activate their cameras when required by departmental policy.

## The Federal Role Debate

The discussion reflects America's traditional tension between federal oversight and local control. While some lawmakers support body cameras in principle, they question federal involvement in local law enforcement.

State-level oversight may offer a middle ground. Several states, including Utah, Kansas, and Mississippi, are developing legislation to regulate body camera use. New Jersey's pending bill would require all state and local officers to wear cameras under attorney general guidelines.

Evesham Police Chief Christopher Chew advocates for consistent national standards: "Federal implementation should establish clear country-wide expectations while respecting local needs."

As body camera technology continues to proliferate among law enforcement agencies, finding the right balance between federal oversight and local autonomy remains crucial for ensuring both accountability and effectiveness.

TALLAHASSEE, Fla. -- While hawksbill turtles are not the only marine turtles endangered by the destabilizing effects of climate change, a recent study by researchers at Florida State University indicates that this critically endangered species is particularly vulnerable.

The study, published in the journal PLOS ONE, was conducted by FSU's Department of Earth, Ocean, and Atmospheric Science. It suggests that projected increases in air temperatures, rainfall, and intense solar radiation could significantly reduce hatching success for hawksbills at several major nesting beaches.

Historically, Earth has experienced numerous climate shifts. However, researchers point out that today's rapid climate changes, combined with unrestrained human development, pose unprecedented threats to hawksbills and other marine turtles.

"Marine turtles have existed for millions of years and have adapted to significant climatic changes during that time," said Mariana Fuentes, Assistant Professor of Oceanography and co-author of the study. "In the past, they adapted by shifting their nesting grounds and seasons to align with more favorable conditions. However, increasing threats to nesting habitats from coastal construction, storms, and rising sea levels are jeopardizing their ability to adapt."

To assess the impact of climate change on hawksbill hatching success, FSU researchers analyzed over 5,000 nests from five Brazilian beaches, where most regional hawksbill nesting occurs. The team focused on five climatic variables—air temperature, rainfall, humidity, solar radiation, and wind speed—to develop a comprehensive model of the subtle effects of a changing climate on the sensitive incubation process.

"There is a lack of research on how climate change might affect hawksbills, especially this population," said Natalie Montero, a former FSU graduate student who led the study. "We chose to investigate the impact on hatchling production because significant changes in the number of baby marine turtles born can dramatically affect population stability."

As reptiles, marine turtles rely on external heat sources for body temperature regulation, making hawksbills and their relatives particularly sensitive to air temperature. This sensitivity is most evident in marine turtle nests, where extreme temperature fluctuations can influence egg incubation, dictate sex ratios, and determine hatching success.

For some marine turtle species, rising temperatures might not necessarily result in less successful incubation. For instance, a study by Montero and Fuentes published earlier this year showed that for loggerhead turtles on the temperate nesting beaches of North Florida, changing conditions might lead to potential short-term increases in hatching success by 1 to 7.6 percent.

However, the outlook for hawksbills is less promising. Montero and Fuentes found that rising air temperatures, coupled with increased rainfall and solar radiation, are projected to reduce overall hatching success at Brazilian nesting sites by up to 11 percent by 2100. Elevated temperatures may warm nests beyond the threshold for healthy incubation, while increased rainfall could saturate the soil and suffocate the embryos.

Even if the turtles manage to incubate successfully and hatch, they face the challenge of heightened solar radiation, which could heat the sand to the point of causing the nests to collapse—a major hazard for hatchlings as they make their way to the sea.

Although the future might seem bleak for this already dwindling species, Montero believes there is still time for humans to mitigate the impact.

"Humans can support marine turtles in numerous ways," she said. "Reducing coastal construction and protecting more coastal habitat will help ensure that both current and future nesting sites are available. It's also crucial to minimize human impact on dune structures and beach vegetation. Additionally, reducing trash and microplastics on the beach can create a higher quality nesting and incubation environment."

Maria A.G. dei Marcovaldi, Milagros Lopez-Mendilaharsu, Alexsandro S. Santos, and Armando J. B. Santos from the Fundação Pró-Tamar in Brazil contributed to this research. The study was supported by grants from the Sea Turtle License Plate Grants Program.

CONAKRY, Guinea (AP) — Guinea's opposition parties announced on Wednesday that they will not participate in the legislative elections scheduled for February. They intend to push for a delay unless the president withdraws his bid to seek another term. 

The opposition's statement follows last year's massive demonstrations where tens of thousands urged President Alpha Condé not to amend the constitution to allow him a third term. At least nine people were killed during one of the protests in October. 

At least five parties have declared their intent not to take part in the February 16 vote. They have also called for new demonstrations on January 13 to protest both the legislative elections and Condé's proposed constitutional changes. 

"Not only will we not participate in this election, but we will also oppose its occurrence by all legal means, as it is merely a charade," stated Ousmane Gaoual Diallo, spokesperson for the Union of Democratic Forces of Guinea, one of the leading opposition parties. 

"We cannot engage in an election that is rigged, with an electoral commission president whose actions are dictated by President Alpha Condé," added Sidya Touré of the Union of Republican Forces, another opposition leader. 

Despite the opposition's declarations, Presidential adviser Souleymane Keita asserted that the vote will proceed. 

"If the opposition chooses not to participate, they will face the consequences," he said. "We will move forward with the elections on February 16, with or without the opposition." 

Condé's mandate concludes in December 2020, yet he seeks a referendum to enable a third term in the West African nation, which has a population of approximately 12 million. The 81-year-old Condé was first elected to a five-year term in 2010, marking Guinea's initial democratic transition of power since gaining independence from France in 1958. He was re-elected in 2015.

"We never really like having the fifth graders at the middle school, but we did it out of necessity," Wilson said. "Building the new school gave us an opportunity to bring them back into a more appropriate age group."

## Innovative Design

# Populist Leaders Endanger Human Rights, Warns Advocacy Organization

*UNITED NATIONS, Jan 12, 2017 (IPS)* - Human Rights Watch warned that populist leaders pose a dangerous threat to human rights, fueling and justifying intolerance and abuse worldwide, during the launch of their annual global report.

In its 2017 World Report, titled "Demagogues Threaten Human Rights," the advocacy group emphasized the rise of populist leaders and their rhetoric that undermines the global human rights system as one of today's most pressing challenges.

"The rise of populism poses a profound threat to human rights," said Kenneth Roth, Human Rights Watch's Executive Director.

Roth explained that populist leaders, who claim to speak "for the people," treat rights as an "impediment" and scapegoat minority communities to address public discontent and domestic issues.

"Trump and various politicians in Europe seek power through appeals to racism, xenophobia, misogyny, and nativism. They all claim that the public accepts violations of human rights as supposedly necessary to secure jobs, avoid cultural change, or prevent terrorist attacks," he added.

The report highlights how President-elect Trump's campaign embodied this politics of intolerance, addressing Americans' economic frustrations and security fears by proposing controversial policies, including:
- Mass deportation of undocumented immigrants
- Creation of a Muslim registry
- Use of torture

If enacted, these proposals risk not only violating human rights but also undermining the entire human rights protection system.

European leaders have exhibited similar populist tendencies. The UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination noted that the UK's Brexit campaign employed "divisive, anti-immigrant and xenophobic rhetoric," prompting calls for officials to reject such discourse.

Despite some progress in relocating asylum seekers, British Prime Minister Theresa May maintained an anti-rights stance, criticizing "activist left-wing human rights lawyers" and seeking to exempt UK forces abroad from human rights law.

Human Rights Watch emphasized that undermining rights for some threatens rights for all. "You may not like your neighbors, but if you sacrifice their rights today, you jeopardize your own tomorrow," Roth cautioned. "In fact, disregard for human rights offers the likeliest route to tyranny."

The rise of Western populism and muted response to violations has emboldened leaders worldwide:

- China's Xi Jinping has led an unprecedented crackdown on dissent
- Turkey's Erdoğan has crushed political and media opposition
- Burundi's Nkurunziza announced withdrawal from the International Criminal Court
- Syria's Assad and Saudi Arabia's Mohammad Bin Salman continue civilian attacks with apparent impunity

Akshaya Kumar, Human Rights Watch's Deputy UN Director, noted that populist leaders now embrace rather than shy away from anti-rights rhetoric. Examples include:

- Hungary's Viktor Orbán's open Islamophobia and anti-refugee policies
- Philippines' Rodrigo Duterte's explicit endorsement of extrajudicial killings

To combat these trends, Kumar advocates targeting enablers of rights abuses, including financial backers and arms suppliers. Recent successes include Canada's 2006 prohibition of LTTE fundraising and the U.S.'s 2016 suspension of arms sales to Philippine police.

The report emphasizes the crucial role of civil society organizations, media, and governments in defending human rights, particularly as some leaders "buried their heads in the sand, hoping the winds of populism will blow over."

Ultimately, the public bears responsibility for addressing populism and promoting human rights. As Roth concluded, "Values are fragile... A society's culture of respect for human rights needs regular tending, lest the fears of the moment sweep away the wisdom that built democratic rule."

Rainy Roth, a children’s ministry leader in her Montana church, volunteers as a crisis counselor with Crisis Text Line.  From her computer in a small town (population 943), she connects with people, primarily under 25, who are struggling with a variety of issues. This work, she finds, intertwines with her role at church, as both involve supporting and nurturing young people.

As a crisis counselor, Rainy completed a rigorous 34-hour training program, covering topics from active listening techniques to dealing with self-harm, suicide, depression, bullying, and gender/sexual identity.  This prepared her for the challenging but rewarding work ahead.

Rainy’s motivation stems partly from her own childhood experience with undiagnosed anxiety.  In the 1960s, mental health awareness was limited, and her struggles were misunderstood.  Now, she finds solace in being able to tell someone, “I get it,” offering understanding and validation she lacked as a child.

While she helps texters with various challenges, Rainy finds the “active rescues” – intervening when someone expresses imminent plans to harm themselves or others – particularly impactful.  Knowing she played a role in getting someone immediate help is profoundly rewarding. “It’s not only about saving lives,” she explains, “it’s also about letting these individuals know that people care.”

A simple phrase, “You matter,” carries surprising weight for many texters.  Rainy frequently hears, “Wow, I have never heard that before!”  These two words offer reassurance and a sense of belonging, countering negative thoughts and feelings.

The connection she forms with texters is deeply fulfilling.  Hearing them acknowledge her words brings a sense of comfort and, in a way, heals a part of herself that struggled for so long with unnamed fear and anxiety.  Being able to identify with their experiences allows her to help them understand that their feelings are valid and that there is hope for change.

Rainy believes she has become a better and healthier person through her work as a crisis counselor.  Her compassion, combined with the skills she gained through training, allows her to offer support and reassurance, letting those in crisis know that things will ultimately be okay.

# Athens Olympics: A Decade Later - Promise, Pride, and Missed Opportunities

## The Dream Begins
After failing in a bid to host the centennial Olympics in 1996, Greece, founder of the ancient and modern Olympics, was awarded the 2004 Games after defeating favorites Rome. The announcement sparked jubilant celebrations, with the Greek delegation, including then-minister George Papandreou, erupting in joy. The moment was so significant that a DJ-remixed version of the announcement was even released as a single.

## From Euphoria to Reality
However, the initial euphoria quickly gave way to challenges. Athens wasted the first three years of its seven-year preparation period, prompting a warning from the IOC in 2000 to accelerate its efforts or risk losing the Games. This led to a frenzied construction period, with crews working three shifts daily to complete venues just weeks before the opening ceremony.

The Games ultimately cost Greece an estimated $11 billion—double the initial projections. New infrastructure emerged across Athens: trams, highways, and gleaming Olympic venues appeared alongside the city's existing architecture. Banners proudly proclaimed "Welcome Home" during the Games.

## A Decade of Decay
Today, ten years later, the legacy of the 2004 Olympics tells a different story:

- The once-gleaming Olympic venues now largely stand abandoned
- The former canoe and kayak venue has dried up, with spectator seats torn out
- At the Olympic rowing center in Marathon, stray dogs roam among overgrown weeds
- Many venues are used only occasionally for non-sporting events like conferences and weddings

## The Economic Impact
For Greeks who once swelled with pride, the Games have become a source of frustration as the country struggles through:
- A six-year depression
- Record unemployment
- Rising homelessness and poverty

While the Hellenic Olympic Committee maintains that the Games' €8.5 billion cost didn't significantly contribute to Greece's €360 billion debt crisis, critics argue differently.

**Big Health's Daylight App Proven Effective for Generalized Anxiety Disorder in Randomized Controlled Trial**

**SAN FRANCISCO & LONDON – July 29, 2020 –** Big Health, the global leader in digital therapeutics for mental health, and the University of Oxford's Sleep Circadian Neuroscience Institute today announced the publication of a randomized controlled trial (RCT) in the journal *Depression and Anxiety*.  The study demonstrates the efficacy and safety of Big Health's Daylight app in improving symptoms of Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD).

The fully automated smartphone-based program leverages evidence-based cognitive and behavioral techniques to help users manage worry and anxiety.  Trial results revealed that Daylight significantly reduced anxiety symptoms compared to the control group after six weeks.  Impressively, 71% of Daylight users achieved remission of GAD by week 10, compared to just 33% in the control group.  These improvements were maintained even at the 26-week (uncontrolled) follow-up, which coincided with the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic – a period of heightened anxiety globally.

"This trial confirms that Daylight is a safe, effective first-line digital therapeutic for worry and anxiety," said Professor Jasper Smits, PhD, Department of Psychiatry at the University of Texas, Austin.  "The consistent and measurable improvements in mental health observed in Daylight users are significant and meaningful, demonstrating the potential of this software to offer relief to those suffering from worry, anxiety, and related conditions."

Anxiety is the most prevalent mental health issue in the United States, affecting over 40 million adults annually.  GAD, characterized by excessive and difficult-to-control worry accompanied by physical symptoms and functional impairment, affects 5-6% of the population in the UK and US, respectively. The COVID-19 pandemic has further exacerbated these challenges, with numerous surveys reporting increased rates of anxiety and stress.

"Anxiety and other mental health challenges cause immense distress globally, yet access to effective solutions remains limited due to stigma and the constraints of in-person care, further compounded by the pandemic," explained Dr. Jenna Carl, vice president of clinical development and medical affairs at Big Health. "These study results confirm Daylight's meaningful impact and its potential to support millions in achieving better mental health, particularly those with limited access to traditional care."

The trial involved 256 participants randomized to either the Daylight intervention or a control group (who received the intervention later).  Participants met criteria for GAD with moderate to severe symptoms, assessed using established clinical measures (MINI and SCID for diagnosis; GAD-7 for severity). Assessments occurred at baseline, mid-intervention (week 3), post-intervention (week 6, primary endpoint), follow-up (week 10), and long-term follow-up (week 26).

In addition to quantitative results, qualitative feedback from participants was positive, highlighting the app's engaging design, soothing voice guidance, practical tools, and overall effectiveness in managing anxiety.  Participants reported feeling more in control, better equipped to challenge negative thoughts, and more confident in their ability to handle anxiety.

Beyond the primary outcomes on anxiety, the study also found statistically significant improvements in worry, depressive symptoms, sleep difficulty, wellbeing, and quality of life.  The effects of Daylight were consistent across demographic groups and severity levels.

Daylight was developed in collaboration with anxiety experts from Boston University, UCLA, University of Oxford, and the University of Texas at Austin.  The program combines animation, developed by veterans of Pixar and Radiolab, with a calming human voice to create an immersive and personalized experience.  Daylight is Big Health's second digital therapeutic, following the success of Sleepio, its digital sleep improvement program.  Daylight has received CE mark approval, signifying its compliance with EU medical device safety and performance requirements.

Investigators continue to search the properties for more remains and evidence.

CNN’s Eliott C. McLaughlin contributed to this report.

ROME (Reuters) -  Italy is grappling with a severe coronavirus crisis and a deep economic recession.  On Wednesday, President Sergio Mattarella moved swiftly to address the situation, asking former European Central Bank chief Mario Draghi to form a new government.  Mattarella’s action followed the collapse of outgoing Prime Minister Giuseppe Conte’s coalition government on Tuesday evening.  The president stressed the urgency of the situation, warning that Italy risked missing out on over 200 billion euros ($243 billion) in European Union recovery funds if a new government wasn't formed immediately.

However, securing the necessary political support is far from guaranteed. Draghi, nicknamed “Super Mario” for his decisive actions at the ECB, where he famously pledged to do “whatever it takes” to save the euro, had largely been out of the public eye since leaving the ECB in October 2019. # Internet Governance Conference Shifts Focus as US Signals Change

A global conference on Internet governance in Brazil is expected to be less contentious than initially anticipated, following the United States' willingness to relax its control over key Internet functions.

The US has agreed to relinquish oversight of the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN) - a California-based nonprofit responsible for managing domain names - responding to demands from Brazil and other nations following revelations of widespread electronic surveillance.

"The focus has shifted from a political reaction to the NSA allegations toward more constructive criticism and dialogue about the Internet's future," notes William Beer, a São Paulo-based cybersecurity expert.

The Net Mundial conference, a two-day event in São Paulo opening Wednesday under Brazilian President Dilma Rousseff, will address several crucial topics:

- Cybersecurity
- Privacy protection
- Freedom of expression
- Future oversight of the decentralized network

Representatives from diverse nations - including China, Cuba, the United States, and European countries - will participate. However, organizers emphasize that government officials will share equal standing with:

- Internet companies
- Academic institutions
- Technical experts
- Internet user advocacy groups

"All stakeholders deserve equal participation in this multi-stakeholder process," explains Virgilio Almeida, Brazil's IT policy secretary and conference chair.

While the conference isn't expected to produce binding decisions, Almeida suggests it will initiate an important dialogue that will "sow the seeds" for future Internet governance reforms.

## Background and Context

The conference emerges from controversy surrounding NSA surveillance programs, which targeted multiple world leaders, including:

- Brazilian President Dilma Rousseff
- German Chancellor Angela Merkel

These revelations, disclosed by former NSA analyst Edward Snowden, prompted international calls to reduce US control over the Internet - a network originally created 50 years ago to connect American universities with the defense industry.

## ICANN Transition

In a surprising move last month, the US government announced plans to transfer ICANN oversight to an international body by September 2015. This transition comes with one crucial condition: the new organization cannot be under any government's control.

The debate over ICANN's future management likely represents a new point of contention, particularly with nations advocating for multilateral control through organizations like the United Nations.

China, Russia, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan have jointly proposed developing a UN-based Internet code of conduct. However, this proposal - originating from countries known for Internet censorship - is unlikely to gain widespread support at the conference.

"Most participants here favor a multi-stakeholder model for the Internet," Almeida told Reuters. "China prefers a UN treaty approach, but the UN only represents governments."

The bout began with Vanesa starting slowly, allowing Odunayo of Mumbai Maharathi to gain the early advantage. However, as the contest progressed, Vanesa found her rhythm and ultimately triumphed 7-5 in the 57 kg competition. At one stage, she was on the brink of defeat but held her nerve to secure an unassailable 4-2 lead for her team in the tie.

The turning point for UP Dangal came from Asian Champion Abdurakhmonov Bekzod, who played a crucial role in setting up the victory after the two teams were tied 2-2. Bekzod scripted a decisive victory over India's Veer Dev in the 74 kg event, putting UP in the driver's seat after the fifth bout. The Uzbek wrestler dominated his opponent, injuring him smartly and completing a 12-0 rout with over three minutes left in the bout.

Earlier in the match, UP Dangal's Nitin, the hero of the last tie, continued his impressive run with a stunning upset. He defeated World Championship bronze medalist Yatsenko Andrey 4-3 in the 57 kg competition, earning his team's first point. Nitin gained an early lead with a solitary point, but the Azerbaijan wrestler bounced back, winning four points to shift the momentum. In a dramatic finish, Nitin clinched a three-pointer in the dying seconds to secure the win.

**Columbia Generating Station Achieves Record-Breaking Nuclear Energy Production in 2018**

RICHLAND, Wash., Jan. 08, 2019 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Columbia Generating Station, the third-largest electricity generator in Washington State, achieved a historic milestone in 2018, producing more clean nuclear energy than any other year in its 34-year operating history.  Surpassing the previous record set in 2016, Columbia delivered over 9.7 million megawatt-hours of electricity to the Northwest power grid.  This marks the fifth new generation record in the last seven years.

This consistent increase in output since 2011 stems from ongoing maintenance and upgrades, which have added approximately 60 megawatts to Columbia’s capacity, bringing its current output to 1,207 megawatts (gross). This is enough clean energy to power Seattle and a portion of its metropolitan area.

“It’s about mitigating climate change one clean megawatt at a time, while providing reliable, low-cost electricity 24/7 throughout the Northwest,” said Energy Northwest CEO Brad Sawatzke.  “Our team’s outstanding work in enhancing nuclear performance continues to lower electricity costs for consumers.”

Energy Northwest projects an average cost of power for Columbia of 4.2 cents per kilowatt-hour during its 2018-2019 fuel cycle, a significant decrease from 6.3 cents (adjusted for inflation) during the 2010-2011 cycle.  Columbia refuels every two years, leading to higher costs during refueling years and lower costs during full-run years. Therefore, generation costs are measured in two-year averages, as shown below:

**Columbia Generation Station Cost of Power (2010-2019)**

| Fuel Cycle (fiscal years) | Cost Per Kilowatt-Hour |
|---|---|
| FY10-11 | 6.30¢ |
| FY12-13 | 5.75¢ |
| FY14-15 | 5.10¢ |
| FY16-17 | 4.70¢ |
| FY18-19 (Estimate) | 4.20¢ |

This cost-effectiveness compares favorably to 2018 EIA estimates for new generation resources potentially entering service by 2022: 4.8 cents for advanced combined-cycle natural gas, 4.7 cents for solar (including a 1.3 cent taxpayer subsidy), and 3.7 cents for onshore wind (including a 1.1 cent taxpayer subsidy).

Washington State enjoys the lowest retail electricity costs in the United States, averaging 7.25 cents per kilowatt-hour over the past five years, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration.

Since 2012, Columbia has maintained an average capacity factor of 92 percent, significantly exceeding national averages for other energy sources.

HONG KONG (AP) — Seven Hong Kong pro-democracy activists pleaded guilty Thursday to organizing and inciting others to take part in an unauthorized assembly held in 2019, local media reported. The activists appearing in court included Raphael Wong, the former chairman of the League of Social Democrats political party, and Figo Chan, who led the Civil Human Rights Front, a now-disbanded group that organized protests.

"I was protesting based on the principle of civil disobedience. One of the key elements of civil disobedience is to accept the charges. So that is what we are going to do later, to plead guilty," Wong said Thursday ahead of the proceedings. He added, "Another key element is that the people carrying out civil disobedience actions know being jailed is just part of the process. We are not worried about being jailed. Instead, we hope we can achieve democracy after this process."

The activists are the latest to appear in court for charges related to the 2019 anti-government protests that roiled the semiautonomous Chinese territory. The protests were sparked by concerns that Beijing was infringing on the freedoms promised to the former British colony when it was handed to Chinese control in 1997. Beijing responded to the protests by imposing a strict new national security law last year that has effectively criminalized much of the opposition to the government and silenced dissent.

Most of the city’s most prominent activists, including Joshua Wong and Apple Daily founder Jimmy Lai, are currently behind bars. Many of them were prosecuted for taking part in unauthorized protests in 2019. Of the seven defendants on Thursday, only Raphael Wong was not held in custody prior to appearing in court. The other six are currently behind bars after being convicted of other offenses related to their activism.

Local news outlets Ming Pao and Stand News later reported all seven pleaded guilty.

The growing use of body cameras by police departments nationwide has been widely regarded as a positive step toward enhancing accountability and transparency in law enforcement. However, the deployment of these devices without well-defined and comprehensive policies introduces significant risks for both the public and officers. These risks encompass concerns related to privacy, data management and the potential for misuse of the technology.

Body-worn cameras (BWCs) are designed to record video and audio during police interactions with the public. Advocates highlight their potential to provide unbiased evidence in cases involving allegations of misconduct or excessive force. Supporters argue that BWCs can foster trust between communities and law enforcement, reduce the number of complaints, and encourage better behavior among officers. Despite these advantages, privacy concerns remain a central issue in discussions about BWCs. The continuous recording feature of these devices means they can unintentionally capture sensitive information, such as private conversations or scenes inside homes. Without clear guidelines on when cameras should be activated or deactivated, there is a risk that individuals’ privacy could be violated.

Another challenge lies in the absence of standardized rules governing how long footage should be stored and under what circumstances it should be made public. Some jurisdictions have strict policies regarding retention periods and release protocols, while others delegate these decisions to individual departments or officers. This inconsistency creates confusion and undermines the potential benefits of the technology. Furthermore, the lack of uniform policies complicates the management of the massive amounts of data generated by BWCs. Many law enforcement agencies lack the infrastructure to store and analyze such large volumes of footage, straining resources and raising concerns about data security and access control.

The absence of clear guidelines on who can access recordings—whether internal investigators, prosecutors, defense attorneys, or the public—also poses risks. Sensitive information could end up in the wrong hands, potentially leading to misuse. Additionally, there is the issue of bias in how BWC footage is utilized within the criminal justice system. For instance, prosecutors might selectively use clips that support their case while disregarding evidence that exonerates the accused. This selective use of footage can compromise the fairness of legal proceedings.

Police unions have expressed concerns about how BWC recordings might be used against officers during disciplinary actions or internal reviews. Without safeguards to protect officers’ due process rights, there is a risk that footage could be exploited unfairly. Critics also argue that the presence of cameras might influence officer behavior in unpredictable ways. While some officers may become more cautious, others might act more aggressively, believing the camera provides them with a layer of protection.

The impact on community relations is another area of concern. If residents perceive that recordings are not handled transparently or fairly, they may lose trust in both the technology and the broader efforts to improve police accountability. Technological limitations further complicate the issue. For example, camera angles may obscure critical details, microphones might fail to capture important audio, and low-light conditions can render footage unusable.

The SALT deduction, a long-standing provision in the U.S. tax code, allows taxpayers to deduct state and local taxes from their federal income tax.  This, according to tax experts, reduces the overall tax burden, especially for those in high-tax states like New York, California, and New Jersey.  The debate surrounding this deduction, however, has resurfaced with intensity, as lawmakers grapple with its impact on federal revenue and tax fairness.

Those in favor of the SALT deduction argue it prevents double taxation, ensuring taxpayers aren't taxed twice on the same income.  Eliminating or capping the deduction, they contend, would disproportionately affect residents of high-tax states, who already contribute significantly to federal coffers.  Lawmakers representing these states have been vocal, arguing that the SALT deduction is essential for economic stability and preventing an outflow of wealthier residents.

Opponents, on the other hand, criticize the deduction, saying it mostly benefits wealthier individuals who itemize and own expensive homes in high-tax areas. These taxpayers, they argue, are effectively subsidized by residents of low-tax states who don’t get such deductions.  Critics also say that unlimited SALT deductions can distort incentives for state-level policymakers to manage finances responsibly.

The 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA) placed a $10,000 cap on the SALT deduction, significantly limiting its benefits, especially for taxpayers in high-tax states. This change sparked outcry from lawmakers representing these regions, who argued it unfairly targeted their constituents. Attempts to repeal or raise the cap have seen mixed success in Congress due to disagreements over its impact on government revenue.

Those who support keeping the cap argue it closes loopholes favoring the wealthy and generates needed revenue for federal programs.  They want a fairer distribution of tax burdens by curtailing excessive deductions enjoyed by affluent taxpayers in high-cost areas.

Recent discussions about fully reinstating SALT deductibility have reignited heated debates across party lines, as legislators weigh various policy considerations during budget negotiations. The Biden administration’s infrastructure bill included provisions to partially restore SALT deductions but faced opposition from Republicans concerned about increasing deficits.

As Congress continues negotiating future tax policy changes, advocates on both sides remain steadfast, presenting arguments for their positions on whether to keep or modify the limitations on SALT deductions under current law.  The ultimate resolution may involve balancing fairness concerns with the need to increase revenue for essential public services.

The word "politics" often evokes exasperation, heated arguments, and fractured relationships in our deeply divided world. Many of us withdraw into echo chambers, surrounding ourselves with those who share our views, avoiding conversations that might challenge our perspectives. But at what cost? Is this self-imposed isolation truly serving us, or is it stifling the very dialogue needed to build understanding and foster progress?

The reluctance to discuss politics now permeates all aspects of life, from family dinners to workplace interactions. We tread carefully, sidestepping controversial topics for fear of sparking conflict. Yet, this avoidance creates a vacuum, enabling misinformation to spread unchecked, eroding trust, and making common ground harder to find.

It's time to dispel the myth that politics is an untouchable topic. At its essence, politics governs the decisions shaping our communities, nations, and the world. It reflects the values we cherish and the future we envision. Opting out of these conversations doesn’t equate to neutrality—it’s a passive disengagement that leaves critical decisions in the hands of others.

Reintegrating political discourse into our lives won’t come without challenges. It demands courage, empathy, and the willingness to listen to opposing viewpoints. It requires stepping outside our comfort zones to engage in meaningful dialogue, even with those we disagree with.

At the heart of productive political conversations is our shared humanity. Despite differing opinions, most of us desire similar outcomes: safety, opportunity, and a brighter future for ourselves and our communities. Recognizing these shared aspirations can provide the foundation for respectful exchanges.

To shift away from the divisive "us versus them" mindset, it’s essential to respect opposing viewpoints as valid, even if they conflict with our beliefs. Respect doesn’t mean surrendering our convictions but acknowledging that others’ perspectives stem from their own experiences and values.

Listening is fundamental. True listening goes beyond hearing words—it’s about understanding the motivations and concerns behind them. It requires setting aside biases and making a genuine effort to see the world through another’s lens.

Empathy is equally vital.

Nigeria's oil sector contribution to GDP plummeted by 6.63 percent, sparking concerns about the nation's economic health.  A new economic report reveals a significant contraction in the oil sector's contribution to Nigeria's Gross Domestic Product (GDP), a troubling development given the industry's longstanding role as a cornerstone of the Nigerian economy.

Data published by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) paints a stark picture: the oil sector's GDP contribution dwindled to a mere 7.35 percent in the second quarter of this year, a sharp decline from 13.98 percent during the same period last year. This downturn is attributed to a confluence of factors, including volatile global oil prices and fluctuating production levels.

Experts warn that this diminished contribution could have profound ramifications for Nigeria's overall economic stability.  Given that oil revenues traditionally constitute a substantial portion of government income, any contraction in this sector inevitably impacts public finances and expenditures on vital social services.

Analysts are urging the Nigerian government to proactively diversify its economy, lessening its dependence on oil exports and channeling resources into burgeoning sectors such as agriculture, manufacturing, and technology. Such a strategic shift would not only mitigate vulnerability to the vagaries of global oil markets but also cultivate new avenues for economic expansion and job creation.

This decline comes at a precarious moment for Nigeria, as the nation grapples with a multitude of economic woes, including soaring inflation, currency depreciation, and escalating unemployment.  These challenges underscore the pressing need for structural reforms designed to foster sustainable economic growth and reduce reliance on volatile sectors like oil.

Several economists contend that tackling corruption and bolstering governance are paramount to attracting foreign investment into non-oil sectors. Enhanced transparency and accountability measures can bolster investor confidence and create a fertile ground for business expansion beyond traditional industries.

Despite these headwinds, glimmers of resilience persist within certain segments of the Nigerian economy. The agricultural sector, for instance, exhibits promising growth potential, fueled by increased investments in modern farming techniques and value-added processing.

Experts suggest that capitalizing on these strengths, coupled with fostering innovation and entrepreneurship, could help mitigate the impact of the oil sector's dwindling contribution on overall GDP performance.

Government officials have acknowledged the imperative for comprehensive reform initiatives aimed at diversifying the Nigerian economy while ensuring inclusive growth that benefits all citizens across the nation's diverse regions.

President Muhammadu Buhari recently articulated his administration's commitment to implementing policies that catalyze economic transformation through targeted interventions designed to bolster productivity across key sectors, including infrastructure development, educational enhancement programs, and investment promotion initiatives.

Political Crisis in Puerto Rico: Governor Ricardo Rosselló Resigns

Background and Causes
San Juan, Puerto Rico – Governor Ricardo Rosselló of Puerto Rico announced his resignation in 2025, effective August 2nd. This decision came after two weeks of large-scale protests and public outrage on the island. The protests were initially sparked by the leak of private chat messages between Rosselló and his inner circle, which were filled with sexist, homophobic, and offensive remarks, as well as potential illegal activities.

Outbreak of Protests and Public Response
The leaked chat messages ignited widespread anger among the Puerto Rican public, especially when combined with long-standing issues of government corruption, economic struggles, and the inefficient recovery from Hurricane Maria. Protests spread rapidly, with people from various sectors joining in. Demonstrations were lively and filled with music, with widespread calls for Rosselló to resign.

Although Rosselló initially refused to step down, his decision only further fueled the protests. Demonstrators blocked highways, clashed with police, and celebrities such as Ricky Martin and Bad Bunny joined the calls for his resignation. U.S. politicians also began expressing concerns about the political instability in Puerto Rico, fearing it could hinder the island’s post-disaster recovery and economic revival.

The Significance of Rosselló’s Resignation
Ultimately, Rosselló announced his resignation under immense pressure, marking a political victory for the people of Puerto Rico. The public’s actions demonstrated the power of collective protest and underscored the importance of accountability. However, while Rosselló’s resignation has been secured, the political crisis in Puerto Rico is far from over.

Succession Issues and Future Challenges
Under Puerto Rican law, Justice Secretary Wanda Vázquez Garced will become the next governor. However, she also faces criticism for her inaction in corruption cases, with public calls for her resignation as well. This succession issue adds complexity to Puerto Rico's political situation, leaving the future direction of the government uncertain.

Loggerhead sea turtles, magnificent creatures that roam the world's oceans, face an existential threat far greater than plastic pollution or entanglement in fishing gear: climate change.  These ancient mariners, already classified as critically endangered, are particularly vulnerable to the warming planet, and scientists warn that the changing climate could deliver a knockout blow to their dwindling populations.

The sex of sea turtle hatchlings is determined by the temperature of the sand in which their eggs incubate. Warmer sands produce more females, while cooler sands produce more males.  With rising global temperatures, beaches are becoming increasingly hotter, resulting in a skewed sex ratio heavily biased towards females.  This imbalance threatens the reproductive viability of loggerheads, pushing them closer to the brink of extinction.

A recent study published in the journal Nature Climate Change paints a grim picture for loggerhead turtles in the face of escalating climate change.  Researchers utilized sophisticated climate models to project the future sex ratios of loggerhead populations under different warming scenarios.  The results are alarming, indicating a significant decline in male hatchlings in the coming decades.  In some regions, the proportion of male hatchlings could drop to a mere 1% by the end of the century.

This dramatic shift in sex ratios has profound implications for the long-term survival of loggerheads.  A scarcity of males limits breeding opportunities, reducing genetic diversity and making the population more susceptible to diseases and environmental changes.  Without sufficient males to fertilize the overwhelming number of females, the reproductive output of the population plummets, jeopardizing the future of the species.

The study's findings underscore the urgency of addressing climate change to protect vulnerable species like loggerhead sea turtles.  The researchers emphasize the need for immediate and decisive action to mitigate greenhouse gas emissions and curb the warming trend.  Delaying action will only exacerbate the problem and further endanger these magnificent creatures.

Beyond the skewed sex ratios, rising sea levels also pose a significant threat to loggerhead nesting sites.  As sea levels rise, beaches are inundated, eroding nesting habitats and submerging existing nests.  This loss of nesting grounds reduces the available space for females to lay their eggs, further hindering reproduction and exacerbating the population decline.

The warming oceans also disrupt the delicate balance of marine ecosystems, impacting the availability of loggerheads' primary food sources.  Changes in ocean currents and water temperatures can affect the distribution and abundance of prey species, making it more challenging for loggerheads to find sufficient food.  This nutritional stress can weaken the turtles, making them more susceptible to diseases and other threats.

The cumulative effects of these climate-driven challenges paint a bleak future for loggerhead sea turtles.  Without intervention, these ancient mariners face a dire predicament, with their populations potentially spiraling towards extinction.  The urgency of the situation calls for a concerted global effort to combat climate change and protect these magnificent creatures and the delicate ecosystems they inhabit.

Conservation efforts are underway to mitigate the impacts of climate change on loggerhead turtles.  Researchers are exploring innovative strategies such as shading nests to reduce incubation temperatures and relocating nests to higher ground to avoid inundation from rising sea levels.  These efforts offer a glimmer of hope, but their long-term success hinges on addressing the root cause of the problem: climate change.

Protecting loggerhead sea turtles requires a multi-pronged approach that includes both mitigating climate change and implementing targeted conservation measures.  Reducing greenhouse gas emissions through transitioning to renewable energy sources, improving energy efficiency, and promoting sustainable land use practices are crucial steps towards curbing the warming trend.

In addition to these global efforts, local conservation initiatives play a vital role in protecting loggerhead nesting sites.  Protecting and restoring coastal habitats, reducing light pollution that disorients hatchlings, and implementing fishing regulations to minimize bycatch are essential measures to safeguard these vulnerable populations.

The fate of loggerhead sea turtles hangs in the balance.

Traveling with a crying baby on a plane can be a daunting experience for any parent. The confined space, the pressure changes, and the general unease of infants in unfamiliar environments can turn a pleasant journey into a stressful ordeal. However, with a little preparation and some tried-and-true strategies, parents can not only manage their baby's discomfort but also minimize the impact on fellow passengers. Here are 32 tips to help you survive—and thrive—during your next flight with a crying infant.

First, choose your seat wisely. If possible, opt for seats near the back of the plane, where there is often more space and fewer passengers are directly affected by noise. Additionally, consider booking a bulkhead seat for extra legroom and a bassinet option. If you're traveling with a partner, request adjacent seats so you can take turns soothing the baby and resting.

Before the flight, ensure your baby is well-fed and has a fresh diaper. A comfortable and content baby is less likely to cry. Pack plenty of snacks and formula if you’re bottle-feeding, and don’t forget a change of clothes for both you and your baby. The key is to anticipate and address basic needs before they become issues.

Noise-canceling headphones or earbuds designed for babies can be a lifesaver. These can help dampen the noise of the plane and make the environment less overwhelming. Bring a white noise machine or play calming music to create a soothing atmosphere. If your baby uses a pacifier, have several on hand as they can provide immediate comfort.

During takeoff and landing, offer your baby something to suck on, such as a bottle, breast, or pacifier. This can help equalize the pressure in their ears and reduce discomfort. If your baby is prone to motion sickness, try feeding them a light snack about an hour before takeoff to settle their stomach.

Engage your baby with toys, books, and activities. Bring a variety of small, quiet toys to keep them entertained.

In a dramatic session that delved into the darker corners of digital espionage, the U.S. Congress convened a hearing to address allegations of spyware companies bribing teenagers to install surveillance software on their devices. The testimony, which spanned several hours, brought to light the unsettling practices that some firms employ to infiltrate private networks and gather sensitive data.

The hearing, held by the House Committee on Oversight and Reform, was led by Chairwoman Carolyn B. Maloney, who opened the session by emphasizing the gravity of the situation. "The allegations we are examining today are not only a violation of privacy but also a serious threat to national security," Maloney stated. The committee heard from a panel of experts, including cybersecurity professionals, former intelligence officials, and affected teens.

One of the key witnesses was Alex Johnson, a 17-year-old high school student from Texas who testified about his experience with a spyware company. Johnson recounted how he was offered a significant sum of money to install software on his and his friends' devices. "They told me it was a simple app to test for bugs, but it turned out to be a lot more," Johnson said, his voice trembling. "I didn't realize the implications until it was too late."

The spyware in question, known as "ShadowEye," was allegedly used to monitor communications, track locations, and even access private files. Johnson's testimony was corroborated by several of his peers, who also took the stand to share their stories. The teens described feeling coerced and misled, with some even threatened if they refused the offer.

Dr. Sarah Thompson, a cybersecurity expert from Stanford University, provided a technical analysis of the spyware. "ShadowEye is a sophisticated piece of malware designed to evade detection and operate covertly," Thompson explained. "It can bypass most security protocols and has the capability to exfiltrate large amounts of data without the user's knowledge."

The committee also heard from former CIA analyst Michael Carter, who testified about the broader implications of such activities. "The use of teenagers to spread spyware is a concerning trend that exploits the vulnerability of young people," Carter said. "It not only compromises individual privacy but also poses a significant risk to corporate and government networks."

Representatives from several major tech companies, including Apple and Google, were called to testify about their efforts to combat spyware. Apple's Senior Director of Security, Lisa Jackson, stated that the company has taken aggressive measures to detect and remove malicious software from its ecosystem. "We have a zero-tolerance policy for any apps that violate our guidelines," Jackson said.

In the depths of winter, January 25th beckons coffee enthusiasts and spirit aficionados alike to raise their glass-handled mugs in celebration of National Irish Coffee Day, honoring one of the most beloved warm cocktails in existence.

The story of Irish Coffee dates back to 1943 when Joe Sheridan, a chef at Foynes Port near Limerick, Ireland, created this comforting concoction for American passengers whose flight had been turned back due to harsh weather conditions.

The drink made its way to America in 1952, when San Francisco Chronicle travel writer Stanton Delaplane introduced it to Jack Koeppler, owner of the Buena Vista Café. Together, they worked tirelessly to recreate Sheridan's original recipe, eventually perfecting the technique of floating the cream on top.

Today, the Buena Vista Café serves up to 2,000 Irish Coffees daily, making it the largest single consumer of Irish whiskey in the United States, a testament to the drink's enduring popularity.

The beauty of Irish Coffee lies in its simplicity: hot coffee, Irish whiskey, brown sugar, and lightly whipped cream. Yet, achieving the perfect balance requires attention to detail and proper technique.

To create this classic drink at home, start with a pre-warmed glass mug – this ensures the coffee stays hot longer and helps the brown sugar dissolve more readily.

Fill the mug about three-quarters full with freshly brewed, strong hot coffee. Traditional recipes call for robust coffee to stand up to the whiskey's bold character.

Add two teaspoons of brown sugar and stir until completely dissolved. The sugar not only sweetens the drink but also helps the cream float on top.

Pour in a measure (about 1 ounce) of quality Irish whiskey. Jameson is a popular choice, though Bushmills or Powers will work beautifully as well.

The crown jewel of Irish Coffee is its cream top. Lightly whip fresh heavy cream until it thickens slightly but still pours smoothly – it should have the consistency of warm honey.

Using the back of a spoon, slowly pour the cream over the coffee mixture. When done correctly, the cream will float atop the coffee, creating distinct layers that make Irish Coffee such a visual and gustatory delight.

The proper way to enjoy this warming beverage is to sip the hot coffee through the cool cream, creating a perfect harmony of temperatures and textures in each mouthful.

The Miami Marlins suffered another heartbreaking defeat, this time a 7-2 loss to the visiting Atlanta Braves, marking their second extra-inning stumble in as many games.  A disastrous tenth inning saw the Marlins' bullpen implode, surrendering five runs and extinguishing any hope of securing a victory. This latest setback underscores the Marlins' ongoing struggles in close contests and casts a shadow over their recent progress.

The game began as a tightly contested pitchers' duel, with both starters effectively neutralizing the opposing lineups.  Miami's Sandy Alcantara delivered another stellar performance, pitching seven scoreless innings, scattering just four hits and striking out eight. Atlanta's Spencer Strider matched Alcantara's dominance, holding the Marlins scoreless through six innings while fanning nine.

The scoreless deadlock finally broke in the seventh when Atlanta's Ozzie Albies launched a solo home run off reliever Tanner Scott, giving the Braves a 1-0 lead.  Miami responded in the bottom half of the inning, tying the game on a sacrifice fly by Bryan De La Cruz.  The game remained knotted at 1-1 through nine innings, setting the stage for extra innings and the eventual unraveling of the Marlins' bullpen.

With the automatic runner placed on second base in the tenth, the Braves quickly capitalized on the scoring opportunity.  A sacrifice bunt advanced the runner to third, setting up an RBI single by Matt Olson that gave Atlanta a 2-1 lead.  The Marlins' woes were compounded by a series of walks, a hit batter, and a wild pitch, culminating in a grand slam by Marcell Ozuna that put the game out of reach.

The Marlins managed to score a single run in the bottom of the tenth, but it was too little, too late.  The final score of 7-2 reflected the lopsided nature of the extra-inning meltdown, leaving the Marlins to grapple with another frustrating loss.

The Marlins' struggles in extra innings have become a recurring theme this season, raising concerns about their ability to close out tight games.  This latest defeat highlighted the vulnerabilities of their bullpen, which has been a source of inconsistency throughout the year.  The Marlins will need to address these issues if they hope to contend in the highly competitive National League East.
